paragraphs: Friend, here's what sits heavy on me about this one. The people in Nazareth heard wisdom and saw miracles, and they were astonished (Mark 6:2). But they stopped at "Isn't this the carpenter?" (Mark 6:3). They knew Jesus so well that they never let Him be who He really was.

That's the trap, and it can catch any of us. We can know the facts and still hold Jesus at arm's length, because He feels too familiar. When Jesus says a prophet is without honor in his hometown, among his relatives and in his own household (Mark 6:4), He's telling us what happens when familiarity wins. The text says He was amazed at their unbelief (Mark 6:6), and I don't take that lightly.

So baker, don't let a story you've heard a hundred times go flat on you. Come to Jesus like you've never met Him, with open hands and open ears. And notice that He didn't quit. He kept going from village to village, teaching the people (Mark 6:6), so His Word is still out there for anyone who will listen.
